build_spec:
# Email Triage — Build Specification

## Overview

Build a twice-daily email triage daemon. The core deliverable is a short classification summary delivered to the operator's channel — no full email bodies, no storage of content, read-only Gmail access.

This is a scheduled script (not a persistent daemon). LaunchDaemons fire it at two configured times per day; the script fetches, classifies, summarises, and exits.

---

## File Layout

```
scripts/
  email_triage.py          ← main CLI: run | status
  email-triage-cron.sh     ← cron trigger (calls email_triage.py run)
workspace/
  email_triage/
    config.json            ← operator config (created on first run if absent)
    runs/                  ← per-run result files
      YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.json
```

All paths are relative to the bot's workspace root (~/.openclaw/workspace/).

---

## Default config (workspace/email_triage/config.json)

Created on first run if absent:

```json
{
  "schedule_times": ["07:30", "13:00"],
  "max_emails_per_run": 25,
  "archive_promotional": false,
  "urgent_senders": [],
  "category_overrides": {}
}
```

---

## Auth: reading Gmail token

Read from openclaw.json → integrations.gmail.token OR the legacy GOG path (openclaw.json → auth.profiles["google_workspace:*"].token).  The email-integration app (p-341576fa) documents the canonical read path; mirror it.

```python
oc = json.loads(Path("/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/openclaw.json").read_text())
# New gmail skill path (post-V2.1-3):
gmail_cfg = oc.get("integrations", {}).get("gmail", {})
token_dict = gmail_cfg.get("token") or {}
access_token = token_dict.get("access_token", "")
# Fallback: GOG auth profile
if not access_token:
    profiles = (oc.get("auth") or {}).get("profiles") or {}
    for k, v in profiles.items():
        if k.startswith("google_workspace:") and isinstance(v, dict):
            inner = v.get("token") or {}
            access_token = inner.get("access_token", "")
            if access_token:
                break
```

If no token after both paths: emit TRIAGE_FAILED: gmail-not-configured and exit 1.

---

## Fetching unread emails

Gmail API v1: list messages, fetch metadata for each.

```python
import base64, urllib.request, json

LIST_URL = "https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages"
MSG_URL  = "https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/{id}"

def gmail_get(url, token):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read())

def fetch_unread(token, max_emails):
    params = urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": "is:unread in:inbox", "maxResults": max_emails})
    data = gmail_get(f"{LIST_URL}?{params}", token)
    ids = [m["id"] for m in data.get("messages", [])]
    emails = []
    for msg_id in ids:
        msg = gmail_get(f"{MSG_URL.format(id=msg_id)}?format=metadata&metadataHeaders=From&metadataHeaders=Subject", token)
        headers = {h["name"].lower(): h["value"] for h in msg.get("payload", {}).get("headers", [])}
        # Body snippet — first 200 chars
        snippet = msg.get("snippet", "")[:200]
        emails.append({
            "id": msg_id,
            "from_addr": headers.get("from", ""),
            "subject": headers.get("subject", ""),
            "snippet": snippet,
        })
    return emails
```

---

## Classification

Send to the Anthropic API using the bot's key (read from openclaw.json → auth.profiles or env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

Model: claude-haiku-3-5 (low cost; classification is simple).
Max tokens: 1024.

### Classifier prompt

```
You are an email triage assistant. Given a list of emails (sender, subject, snippet), classify each one.

For each email return a JSON array where each object has:
  "id": the email id (exact string, unchanged)
  "urgency": one of urgent | important | routine | promotional | spam-likely
  "category": one of financial | legal | family | work-project | vendor | news | personal | other
  "action": one of reply-now | reply-today | can-wait | can-ignore | archive

Urgency rules:
- urgent: needs a response today or involves time-sensitive action
- important: worth reading soon but not blocking
- routine: normal correspondence, no time pressure
- promotional: marketing, newsletters, offers
- spam-likely: unsolicited, suspicious, or clearly junk

Return ONLY the JSON array. No prose, no markdown fences.
```

User message: JSON array of {id, from_addr, subject, snippet} for all emails in this run.

### Parsing

Expect a JSON array. If parsing fails: fall back to heuristic classification (see below) and emit TRIAGE_PARTIAL:.

### Heuristic fallback (used when LLM fails or API key missing)

- promotional if subject contains: unsubscribe, newsletter, % off, deal, sale, offer
- spam-likely if subject/from contains: noreply@, no-reply@, donotreply@
- urgent if from_addr is in urgent_senders config
- important if subject contains: urgent, action required, deadline, invoice, payment due
- routine otherwise

category: financial if sender domain or subject matches: bank, invoice, payment, receipt, statement, tax
legal: contract, agreement, legal, attorney, counsel
family: from urgent_senders (non-vendor) or personal email domains
others: use other as default

---

## Config override application

Apply after LLM classification:
1. If from_addr is in config.urgent_senders → override urgency to urgent, action to reply-now
2. If any key in config.category_overrides matches from_addr (substring match, case-insensitive) → override category

---

## Message composition

```
Email triage — {date} {time}

{N} emails | {urgent_count} urgent, {important_count} important, {routine_count} routine, {promo_count} promotional

Urgent
• {sender_name} — {subject}
• {sender_name} — {subject}

Important
• {sender_name} — {subject}
```

Rules:
- Only show sections with at least one email
- If urgent_count == 0: show "Nothing urgent."
- If total <= 1: "Only 1 unread email. No triage needed."
- sender_name: extract display name from "Name <email>" format; fall back to domain only
- Omit routine/promotional/spam sections from the message (operator doesn't need to act on them)

---

## Delivery

Use the canonical delivery pattern (docs/spec-gallery-delivery-convention-2026-06-11.md; reference implementation in docs/reference/capabilities/template/scripts/example_script.py): resolve (channel, target) from the pod network.json — which lives ONLY at the canonical shared path `/Users/Shared/evolve/network.json` (read it there; it is NOT at `/Users/<bot>/.openclaw/network.json` and NOT in the workspace — copy the `SHARED_DIR = Path('/Users/Shared/evolve')` constant and `load_network()` helper from docs/reference/capabilities/template/scripts/example_script.py verbatim) — reading `bots.<bot_id>.primary_user.external_ids` (channel priority: telegram, whatsapp, signal, imessage, slack, discord, sms, matrix — intersected with the bot's own enabled channels from its openclaw.json `channels.<name>.enabled`, falling back to the best recorded id when there is no overlap so the send fails loudly), then run `openclaw message send --channel=<ch> --target=<target> --message=<text> --json` as the bot user (binary: `shutil.which("openclaw")`, falling back to /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin; cwd = the executing account's pwd-database home, NOT $HOME, so node can resolve its CWD even under sudo-without--H; child PATH prefixed with the CLI's own bin dir so the `#!/usr/bin/env node` entrypoint resolves under launchd's minimal PATH; timeout 60s). Exit code 0 = the channel accepted the send. Never read gateway port/token; never POST to the gateway. On send failure: emit `TRIAGE_FAILED: {date} delivery-error` and exit 1 without writing the run result. If the bot has no recorded delivery route: emit `TRIAGE_SKIPPED: {date} no-delivery-route` and exit 0 without writing the run result.

---

## email-triage-cron.sh

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# email-triage-cron.sh — email triage cron trigger
# Fired by LaunchDaemon at each configured schedule time.

WORKSPACE="/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace"
LOGFILE="/tmp/{bot_id}-email-triage.log"

python3 "$WORKSPACE/scripts/email_triage.py" run \
  >> "$LOGFILE" 2>&1

exit 0
```

Make executable. Register two LaunchDaemons (morning + afternoon).

---

## LaunchDaemon plists

Two plists — one per run time. Write to:
  /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.{bot_id}.email-triage-morning.plist
  /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.{bot_id}.email-triage-afternoon.plist

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN"
  "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key>
  <string>com.{bot_id}.email-triage-morning</string>
  <key>UserName</key>
  <string>{bot_id}</string>
  <key>GroupName</key>
  <string>staff</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/bin/bash</string>
    <string>/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/email-triage-cron.sh</string>
  </array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict>
    <key>TZ</key>
    <string>{time_zone}</string>
  </dict>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
  <dict>
    <key>Hour</key>
    <integer>{morning_hour}</integer>
    <key>Minute</key>
    <integer>{morning_minute}</integer>
  </dict>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key>
  <string>/tmp/{bot_id}-email-triage-out.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
  <string>/tmp/{bot_id}-email-triage-err.log</string>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key>
  <false/>
</dict>
</plist>
```

The afternoon plist mirrors this with Label = email-triage-afternoon and the afternoon Hour/Minute.

---

## Template variables

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{bot_id}` | yes | — | The bot's macOS user ID |
| `{time_zone}` | no | America/Los_Angeles | IANA timezone for LaunchDaemon TZ env |
| `{morning_hour}` | no | 7 | Hour for morning run (derived from schedule_times[0]) |
| `{morning_minute}` | no | 30 | Minute for morning run |
| `{afternoon_hour}` | no | 13 | Hour for afternoon run (derived from schedule_times[1]) |
| `{afternoon_minute}` | no | 0 | Minute for afternoon run |

## Test sequence

After building:

```bash
# 1. Syntax check
python3 -m py_compile scripts/email_triage.py

# 2. Status (before first run)
python3 scripts/email_triage.py status
# Expected: 'No triage run logged today yet.' or similar

# 3. Dry run (no network, no send — uses heuristic fallback on empty)
python3 scripts/email_triage.py run --dry-run
# Expected: exits 0, prints summary or 'no unread emails'

# 4. Executable
test -x scripts/email-triage-cron.sh && echo 'OK: cron script executable'

# 5. Config exists after first run --dry-run
test -f workspace/email_triage/config.json && echo 'OK: config created'
```

All steps must exit 0.
